key_insight: Random data splits can reward recipe memorisation, while provenance-grouped evaluation better tests generalisation to unseen perovskite solar-cell research.
engineering_relevance: Reliable device optimisation requires models that generalise beyond familiar recipes and account for architecture and fabrication alongside absorber chemistry.
method: Map institutional provenance in the Perovskite Database.
Use grouped splits that progressively isolate duplicate devices, publications and institutions.
Benchmark 13 models and analyse feature importance.
evidence_signal: Nearly two-thirds of curated devices share an exact recipe; tree ensembles lead on random splits, but composition-aware neural models excel on unseen institutions and future discoveries.
watch_item: Reliable grouped evaluation depends on accurate recipe, publication and institutional metadata, and does not alone establish prospective experimental success.
paper_title: Provenance-grouped protocol for evaluating machine learning in perovskite photovoltaics
